name: Tonn Ruray Café
improvements: Add a /concepts/tonn-ruray/menu/ secondary page with an illustrative-items disclaimer so the primary menu action completes the visit loop the design task promises.
Add a publishable café frontage or interior photograph when one becomes available — the concept currently relies on typography and the through-the-day card alone.
summary: The café is clearly separated from the apartments: the banner, strip toggle, brand sub-label, warm café identity and case-study notes all state that only the café is being redesigned while the apartment site is left alone and linked honestly. The Gertrude Stein headline and JUN24 menu critique match the live tonnruray.com site. Menu and booking controls use the standard inert placeholder pattern with a hero note explaining the PDF replacement; that is sufficient for publication though a menu secondary page would strengthen the core promise.
verificationNote: Verified open 24 July 2026; café confirmed as the failing half beneath apartment-first billing, with JUN24 menu PDF and no booking.

retirement.reason: The concept was worse than the website it proposed to replace, and all four checks passed it — the same limit the Dundrum Inn exposed a day later. Tonn Ruray is a new business whose site is personal and deliberate: its own shopfront photograph in low golden light, its own food photography, a Gertrude Stein quote on coffee chosen because someone liked it, a hand-drawn squiggle under See the Menu, one consistent dusty-pink and italic-serif identity. The concept deleted the photography for typography on cream, compressed the owners' chosen quote into a grotesk slogan and credited it back to them, replaced their palette with the studio's, rendered all seven of its links as struck-through dead placeholders, and printed a remark about the owners' own room pricing inside the owners' proposed page. Its real gap — a JUN24 menu PDF two years stale and a BOOK NOW that resolves to a contact form — is a maintenance problem that a redesign does not fix.
retirement.falseClaimFound: The published case study and the before-clip alt text both stated that the homepage opens on Sea View Luxury Apartments and nightly rates, with the café second beneath the accommodation. The capture we published shows the opposite: the homepage opens on the café shopfront under the TONN RURAY wordmark with EAT first in the navigation, then the coffee quote, then Fresh local ingredients with a seasonal menu. No apartments or rates appear anywhere in the captured scroll. The first of the three case-study notes — Stop making the café share a hero — rested entirely on that claim. Either the site changed between the research pass and the capture, or the apartment-first reading was wrong from the start; the evidence we hold does not support it. This is a fourth false sourcing claim of the class corrected in 7fd4d73, and that sweep did not catch it.
retirement.evidence: The 24 July 2026 before poster and ten-second clip were removed from public/ with this retirement. They remain retrievable at commit dc87b15 — public/images/tonn-ruray-before.jpg and public/videos/tonn-ruray-before.mp4.
